name: advance

ops.description: Write operations, one flat object per op, run in order. A field marked [ops: ...] applies only to the ops named.

itemId.description: Item id: a UUID or a dash-free hex prefix of 8 to 32 characters.

trigger.description: The trigger to apply: start, complete, block, hold, resume, cancel or reopen. [ops: transition]

summary.description: Optional human-readable summary recorded on the transition. [ops: transition]

credentialRefs.description: Audit labels of the credentials this transition consumed (opaque labels, never secret values): at most 8, each 1 to 128 characters matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-_./]*$. [ops: transition]

select.description: Find-and-claim: claim the best eligible item matching these filters. [ops: claim]

role.description: Role to look in; default queue.

parentId.description: Only direct children of this item.

tags.description: Match items carrying any of these tags.

complexityMax.description: Only items with a complexity of at most this value.

createdAfter.description: Only items created at or after this instant.

createdBefore.description: Only items created at or before this instant.

roleChangedAfter.description: Only items whose role changed at or after this instant.

roleChangedBefore.description: Only items whose role changed at or before this instant.

orderBy.description: Ranking of the matches: priority (default), oldest or newest.

ttlSeconds.description: Claim lifetime in seconds, 1 to 86400; default 900. [ops: claim, heartbeat]

claimRef.description: Opaque caller reference (at most 64 characters), echoed in the result. [ops: claim]

idempotencyKey.description: Optional client key (1-128 chars, needs actor). Resending the same op with the same key returns the stored result.

atomic.description: true: the first failing op rolls back the whole batch. Default false: each op commits on its own.

describe.description: true: return the operations, their parameters and errors instead of running the tool.

description: Move items through their phases and manage who owns them. Each ops[] element has an op: transition (apply a trigger), claim (take an item by id or by selector), release, or heartbeat (extend a held claim). A transition on an item claimed by someone else is not_claim_holder. Call with describe:true for each operation's parameters and errors.
